size.note: Head and body 30-37 cm, ear 5-6 cm, tail 1-3 cm (brief). The build script scales head and body (nose to tail root, measured along the spine since the crouch tilts the body) to 0.33 m; the crouched rabbit stands 0.17 m at the back and 0.23 m to the ear tips.

source.original: FBX in a 7z archive: rigged rabbit (1,700-triangle body plus alpha fur cards and whisker strands), 10 clips, 1K diffuse and normal maps; a European rabbit or hare with long ears

license_detail.source_terms: The OpenGameArt page lists "License(s): CC0"; the archive's License.txt reads "License: CC0 - Public Domain" (Čestmír Dammer). CC0 1.0: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/.
license_detail.note: CC0 places no conditions, so the adopted tiers may ship in client/assets and be relicensed with the project's assets. Credit is kept anyway (README, build script header, GLB asset.copyright).

rig: rodent template R (animalModels.js): BODY hindquarters, CHEST (pivot at the lumbar joint), HEAD and LEG_A (fore pair, pivots at the elbows) children of the chest, LEG_B (hind pair with the long hind feet, pivots at the stifles), TAIL; from the source skin weights; parent pivots in extras.rig. No TAIL_TIP (the tail is a stub) and no EARS part (ears ride with the head).
accuracy_notes: Fur cards and whiskers dropped; posed in the source's resting crouch (Sitting clip frame 1, the only low symmetric pose); ears 0.55x about their base, tail 0.5x; the diffuse texture is sampled per face for its ticking and multiplied onto the brief's darker palette. Reads as a small dark wild cottontail, not a pet bunny or a hare: short dark-rimmed ears, compact body, grey-brown back, warmer nape, pale grey belly and inner forelegs, buff feet, a tiny tail dark above and pale below, dark eye with a pale ring. Still wrong or unchecked: the pose is a sitting crouch with the fore body raised, not a level feeding crouch; the head is large and round (the source is a European rabbit); the ears measure about 4 cm above their joint, at the short end of the brief's 5-6 cm; the eye ring may be too bright; lod1 ears are blades and lod2 is a wedge with ears. A local check of ear length and overall darkness is wanted.
